analyst_view.overall: Early view: Braga are 8th and back to winning after a five-round league drought, beating Famalicão 3-0 and Rio Ave 1-0, but this Monday game comes four days after a Conference League home game against KuPS and eight days after a Taça de Portugal derby at Vitória. Casa Pia are 16th with the fewest goals in the league (6), though they won 2-0 at Estrela and drew at Alverca recently. My research on Casa Pia's own team news is thin, so this view rests mostly on form and fixtures.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean lower: Casa Pia have scored 6 times in 11 games, and Braga's attack has been modest (13 goals) and won its last two league games by 3-0 and 1-0. A tired Braga after a European Thursday points to a controlled, narrow game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, most of them for Braga. That fits a home side that defends deep and a visitor that will have the ball. I found nothing to move it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. Casa Pia's fight against relegation could add some edge, but Braga after a busy European week may not force a high tempo. Without a referee named, I stay with the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.1 shots, 16.4 for Braga. With Braga possibly rotating after KuPS and Casa Pia carrying so little threat, I expect fewer attempts. Rio Ave restricted Braga to a single goal last weekend.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Casa Pia's attack is the league's weakest, which limits their share, and Braga have not been creating many clear chances. I lean slightly lower.
